evidence_quotes.name_asked_and_used: Rep: 'Hi, good afternoon, this is juline with Einstein moving. Am I speaking with Kaleen?' Customer: 'Yes, hi, how are you?' Rep never uses the name again.
evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: No framing given about 10-15 minute timeframe or dependable quote. Rep goes straight into conversation.
evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Never asked. Rep launches into logistics and conversation without the two-concerns opener.
evidence_quotes.concern_led_opening: Rep asks clarifying questions about items but never opens with 'What items in this move are you most concerned about?' or similar concern-led framing.
evidence_quotes.box_count: Asked: 'do you think you would fall within that range?' for 20-30 boxes, customer responds 'about 35 boxes in the garage. And then there's gonna be another one.' Packing question never asked.
evidence_quotes.two_promises: Neither On-Time Guarantee nor No Worries Damage Coverage mentioned at any point in the call.
evidence_quotes.routing_to_walkthrough: Rep: 'By any chance, are you available to do a virtual walkthrough? So it's like a video call just for me to see how large the furniture are as well as the items from the garage. Are you available to do it?' Customer agrees. Rep confirms: 'I'll just send you a text message with a link so just click on that link and then you'll be routed to our video call.'

top_strength: Rep correctly identified that a virtual walkthrough was appropriate for this move (high box count, multiple appliances, ambiguous furniture sizing) and secured customer agreement to proceed, which is the appropriate routing decision for a complex 1-bedroom load.
coaching_note: Before routing to walkthrough, deliver the quid pro quo framing (time commitment + dependable quote promise) and never skip the two-concerns question and Two Promises — these are foundational trust-builders that should land before any detail gathering or routing decision, even on walkthrough-bound calls.
